A1.justification: Both PDFs describe STBLLM. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and rendered figures, support reliable comparison. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model perplexities, seven-task zero-shot accuracies, weight-flipping results and component ablations in the main text and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations and adds GPU runtime, throughput and memory measurements, further pruning-metric comparisons and weight-flipping accuracy results.

M1.justification: v2 introduces a specialized CUDA inference kernel for 1-bit weights with 2:4 sparsity, including index/sign packing and sparse tensor-core multiplication (Section 4.3 and Appendix C). v1 discusses hardware acceleration prospectively without this implemented component. The SI metric, adaptive allocation, residual approximation and non-salient quantization procedures remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Wikitext2, C4, PTB and the same seven zero-shot tasks. The added analyses use existing language-task coverage; sparsity configurations, weight-flipping accuracy measurements and hardware performance sweeps change evaluation settings and measurements without introducing another data domain or language task.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons with ABQ-LLM for runtime and throughput, and CUTLASS and SmoothQuant for memory consumption (Figures 4 and 9). AWQ, previously discussed but not evaluated, appears in the new perplexity comparison in Figure 4(b). The earlier benchmark and ablation comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds fixed 2:4 evaluations and RTX4090 benchmarking with sequence-length sweeps, runtime, TFLOPS and memory metrics. Appendix C also specifies roofline comparisons at M=K=4096 and several N values. The weight-flipping evaluation gains downstream accuracy measurements alongside retained perplexities. Existing benchmark calibration and block-size settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The weight-flipping robustness analysis expands to ARC-easy, BoolQ, HellaSwag and RTE accuracy curves in Figure 1. New Table 7 extends pruning-metric comparisons to PTB and C4, while Appendix C.2 adds analysis of memory and compute bottlenecks. Earlier quantization, allocation, calibration-data and group-size ablations remain present after relocation.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 1 introduces shaded bands around accuracy curves, but neither its caption nor the appendices identifies their statistical meaning or calculation. Neither version specifies corresponding run counts or seeds. The PDFs therefore do not establish whether these bands constitute newly reported statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: The original benchmark tables and flipping-perplexity values are retained, including v1 Table 12 as v2 Table 13. v2 adds accuracy-under-flipping, 2:4 perplexity and hardware results, reporting up to 17.85x speedup and 263.45 TFLOPS in Section 4.3. Table 7 adds comparisons such as SparseGPT 236.03 versus SI 690.76 on LLaMA-2-7B/PTB. These are new comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds quantitative hardware reasoning: six versus eight bits per four-weight group yields 25% storage savings and a theoretical 1.333x memory-bound speedup, alongside roofline-based compute bounds. The original quantization equations, linear-time breakpoint-search argument and Hessian discussion are retained; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion newly present the specialized CUDA kernel as a central contribution, with the introduction claiming 17.85x acceleration over ABQ-LLM. This extends the contribution from structured quantization and prospective deployment benefits to implemented hardware acceleration. The original sub-1-bit compression and accuracy claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking kernel gains to reduced memory traffic and sparse tensor-core capacity, distinguishing decoding from prefilling bottlenecks. Its conclusion replaces the limitation about unexplored 1-bit/2-bit STBLLM settings with non-support for MoE and Mamba models. The earlier federated-learning applicability and associated future-work discussion is removed.

D1.justification: v2 documents kernel encoding, Uint16 indices, Uint8 sign packing and tensor-core processing, and supplies Algorithm 3 for weight flipping. Section 4.1 newly reports post-training times of 1.8 hours for 7B models on RTX4090 and 2.8 hours for 13B models on A6000. It removes v1's promise to release code upon acceptance without providing an STBLLM access link.

R1.justification: Related work is reframed around structured/unstructured pruning and joint pruning-quantization, adding works such as CLIP-Q and OPQ. Hardware positioning expands through ABQ-LLM, ULPPack, NGEMM and QQQ. Removal of the broader-impact section also removes substantial federated-learning, architecture-search and distillation positioning. Bibliographic updates to retained works are separate from these substantive changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting, including an explicit contribution list. v2 adds a hardware subsection and appendix overview, reorganizes the appendices, and removes the broader-impact section. Author information, citation style and algorithm presentation also change, while much of the methodological exposition is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes from a perplexity curve to four accuracy curves with shaded bands. v2 adds hardware comparisons and encoding diagrams in Figures 4-9 and the expanded pruning-metric Table 7. Existing tables and ablation plots are relocated or renumbered, including v1 Figures 4-6 becoming v2 Figures 10-12. Conference formatting and algorithm layouts also change.

improvement.justification: The concrete kernel description and measured efficiency comparisons provide better support for practical deployment than v1's prospective hardware discussion. Expanded metric ablations also improve empirical scrutiny. However, the connection between the six-bit-per-four-weight hardware encoding and the claimed sub-1-bit representation remains unclear, and erroneous appendix interpretations treating higher perplexity as better persist. The evidence supports a net improvement, with substantial limitations remaining.
